title: Nakho-Dagestanian languages | Nakh-Dagestan, Caucasus, Endangered ...
text: Nakho-Dagestanian languages, group of languages spoken in the northeastern Caucasus Mountains. The Nakh division consists of the languages of the Chechen, Ingush, and Bats. The Dagestanian division is more multifarious and includes such groups as the Avar-Andi-Dido languages, the Lak-Dargin (Lak-Dargwa) languages, and the Lezgian languages. See also Dagestanian languages; Nakh languages.

text: Northeast Caucasian languages The Northeast Caucasian languages, also known as Nakh-Daghestanian or East Caucasian languages, form one of the three major indigenous language families of the Caucasus region, comprising 36 distinct languages spoken primarily by approximately 4.3 million people, mainly in Russia, as of 2021.

title: Lak alphabet and language - Omniglot
text: Lak (Лакку маз) Lak is a Nakh-Daghestanian or Northeast Caucasian language spoken in the Dagestan Republic in the Russian Federation. According to the 2010 census, there are about 146,000 speakers of Lak, which is also known as Lakh, Laki or Kazikumukhtsy. It is closely related to Dargwa.

title: Chechen language, alphabet and pronunciation - Omniglot
text: Chechen is part of the small family of Nakh-Daghestanian or Northeast Caucasian languages spoken mainly in the Republic of Chechnya in the Russian Federation by 1.35 million people, according to the 2010 Russian census. There are also some Chechen speakers in Georgia, Germany, Jordan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Syria, Turkey and Uzbekistan.
